config.paper: Yeom et al. 2018 Privacy Risk in Machine Learning

methodology.paper_attack: Yeom et al.'s LOSS membership inference predicts membership when the target model assigns a candidate example unusually low loss; the advantage is linked to the training-vs-held-out generalization gap.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; lower loss predicts membership.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Federated clients locally fine-tune an open-source causal LM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg strategy via run_simulation. Positive and negative worlds differ by whether the target client includes the target sequence. The server/adversary scores the final FL model's average per-token NLL on the target sequence and thresholds the loss using calibration non-members.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The original paper evaluates classical supervised models. This notebook preserves the LOSS decision rule but moves the training process to FedAvg-based causal-LM fine-tuning.
methodology.attacker_observation: Final FL global model probabilities/logits sufficient to compute per-token NLL.

config.paper_source: Mattern et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18462) Neighbourhood Comparison MIA

methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. No reference model is needed: the neighbours are the difficulty calibration. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer and toy single-word neighbour perturbations; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg) with BERT (bert-base-uncased) neighbour generation following Algorithm 1 (n=100, m=1, dropout p=0.7 on the original embedding).
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss so members (loss below neighbours) score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.

config.paper_source: Shi et al. 2024 (ICLR / arXiv:2310.16789) Min-K% Prob reference-free MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of the k% lowest per-token log-probs so members score higher. AUC is the paper's threshold-free headline metric.

config.paper_source: Carlini et al. 2021 (arXiv:2012.07805) zlib-entropy ratio MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only, dividing its log-perplexity by the record's zlib entropy. No reference model is used.
methodology.paper_attack: zlib-entropy ratio MIA: rank candidates by log_perplexity / len(zlib.compress(text)); zlib is a model-independent reference that down-ranks repetitive/boilerplate text.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = -(log_perplexity / zlib_entropy_bits) so members score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Carlini et al. flag fine-tuning as future work, so applying the zlib ratio to a fine-tuned model is a transfer of their pre-training signal. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA
Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.

methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.

config.paper_source: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02751) Window-Based Comparison MIA; repo github.com/Stry233/WBC

methodology.deviation_from_source: The paper's black-box reference/target attack is transferred to a federated fine-tuning threat model. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer with an untrained reference; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and a pre-trained reference model.
methodology.paper_attack: WBC (Window-Based Comparison): form per-token Delta_j = ref NLL - target NLL, slide multiple window sizes over it, each window casts a binary sign vote (sum > 0 => member), and rank by the fraction of member-voting windows ensembled over geometric window sizes. config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).

methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.

config.paper_source: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02751) Window-Based Comparison MIA; repo github.com/Stry233/WBC

methodology.paper_attack: WBC (Window-Based Comparison): form per-token Delta_j = ref NLL - target NLL, slide multiple window sizes over it, each window casts a binary sign vote (sum > 0 => member), and rank by the fraction of member-voting windows ensembled over geometric window sizes. Sign vote beats a mean under heavy-tailed rare-token contamination.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; WBC membership score = fraction of windows with positive summed loss difference (members score higher).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, build Delta_j = reference-model NLL - final-FL-model NLL for the target record (reference = base model before FL) and score it with the WBC sign-vote fraction. Higher fraction => member.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The paper's black-box reference/target attack is transferred to a federated fine-tuning threat model. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer with an untrained reference; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and a pre-trained reference model.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.

config.paper_source: Mattern et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18462) Neighbourhood Comparison MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss so members (loss below neighbours) score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. No reference model is needed: the neighbours are the difficulty calibration. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer and toy single-word neighbour perturbations; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg) with BERT (bert-base-uncased) neighbour generation following Algorithm 1 (n=100, m=1, dropout p=0.7 on the original embedding).
methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.

methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.

Sign vote beats a mean under heavy-tailed rare-token contamination.

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.

No reference model is used.

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.

config.paper_source: Shi et al. 2024 (ICLR / arXiv:2310.16789) Min-K% Prob reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of the k% lowest per-token log-probs so members score higher. AUC is the paper's threshold-free headline metric.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.

config.paper_source: Mattern et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18462) Neighbourhood Comparison MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss so members (loss below neighbours) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. No reference model is needed: the neighbours are the difficulty calibration. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer and toy single-word neighbour perturbations; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg) with BERT (bert-base-uncased) neighbour generation following Algorithm 1 (n=100, m=1, dropout p=0.7 on the original embedding).
methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.

config.paper_source: Mattern et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18462) Neighbourhood Comparison MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss so members (loss below neighbours) score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. No reference model is needed: the neighbours are the difficulty calibration. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer and toy single-word neighbour perturbations; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg) with BERT (bert-base-uncased) neighbour generation following Algorithm 1 (n=100, m=1, dropout p=0.7 on the original embedding).

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.

config.paper_source: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02751) Window-Based Comparison MIA; repo github.com/Stry233/WBC

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; WBC membership score = fraction of windows with positive summed loss difference (members score higher).
methodology.paper_attack: WBC (Window-Based Comparison): form per-token Delta_j = ref NLL - target NLL, slide multiple window sizes over it, each window casts a binary sign vote (sum > 0 => member), and rank by the fraction of member-voting windows ensembled over geometric window sizes. Sign vote beats a mean under heavy-tailed rare-token contamination.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, build Delta_j = reference-model NLL - final-FL-model NLL for the target record (reference = base model before FL) and score it with the WBC sign-vote fraction. Higher fraction => member.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The paper's black-box reference/target attack is transferred to a federated fine-tuning threat model. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer with an untrained reference; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and a pre-trained reference model.

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.

methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of the k% lowest per-token log-probs so members score higher. AUC is the paper's threshold-free headline metric.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.

config.paper_source: Mattern et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18462) Neighbourhood Comparison MIA

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss so members (loss below neighbours) score higher.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.

config.paper_source: Shi et al. 2024 (ICLR / arXiv:2310.16789) Min-K% Prob reference-free MIA

methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.

config.paper_source: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02751) Window-Based Comparison MIA; repo github.com/Stry233/WBC

methodology.deviation_from_source: The paper's black-box reference/target attack is transferred to a federated fine-tuning threat model. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer with an untrained reference; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and a pre-trained reference model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; WBC membership score = fraction of windows with positive summed loss difference (members score higher).
methodology.paper_attack: WBC (Window-Based Comparison): form per-token Delta_j = ref NLL - target NLL, slide multiple window sizes over it, each window casts a binary sign vote (sum > 0 => member), and rank by the fraction of member-voting windows ensembled over geometric window sizes. Sign vote beats a mean under heavy-tailed rare-token contamination.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, build Delta_j = reference-model NLL - final-FL-model NLL for the target record (reference = base model before FL) and score it with the WBC sign-vote fraction. Higher fraction => member.

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.

methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by generating neighbours and taking mean_neighbour_loss - target_loss. No reference model is used.

methodology.paper_attack: Neighbourhood comparison MIA: for target x, generate n near-identical neighbours via BERT masked-LM single-word (m=1) substitution, then predict member when L(x) is substantially below the mean neighbour loss (Eq. 3). Reference-model-free: neighbours replace the reference model.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The attack was designed for the fine-tuning setting, so applying it to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.
methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.

The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.

config.paper_source: Xie et al. 2024 (EMNLP, arXiv:2406.15968) ReCaLL relative conditional log-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = LL(x|P) / LL(x) (ReCaLL ratio) so members score higher.
methodology.paper_attack: ReCaLL: build a fixed prefix P from n non-member shots; score a target x by ReCaLL(x) = LL(x|P) / LL(x). Conditioning on the non-member prefix depresses the LL more for members, so members get higher ratios (typically > 1). Reference-model-free, inference-time only.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by computing LL(x) and LL(x|P) with a fixed non-member prefix P disjoint from every client corpus, then take the ratio. No reference model is used.
methodology.deviation_from_source: ReCaLL targets single-epoch pre-training; the paper notes multi-epoch fine-tuning is an easier MIA regime, so the signal transfers with equal or stronger effect. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose conditional log-likelihood drops more for memorized (member) tokens; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.

config.paper_source: Zhang et al. 2025 (ICLR / arXiv:2404.02936) Min-K%++ reference-free MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.

config.paper_source: Shi et al. 2024 (ICLR / arXiv:2310.16789) Min-K% Prob reference-free MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of the k% lowest per-token log-probs so members score higher. AUC is the paper's threshold-free headline metric.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.

config.paper_source: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.02751) Window-Based Comparison MIA; repo github.com/Stry233/WBC

methodology.paper_attack: WBC (Window-Based Comparison): form per-token Delta_j = ref NLL - target NLL, slide multiple window sizes over it, each window casts a binary sign vote (sum > 0 => member), and rank by the fraction of member-voting windows ensembled over geometric window sizes. Sign vote beats a mean under heavy-tailed rare-token contamination.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The paper's black-box reference/target attack is transferred to a federated fine-tuning threat model. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer with an untrained reference; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and a pre-trained reference model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; WBC membership score = fraction of windows with positive summed loss difference (members score higher).

config.paper_source: Kaneko et al. 2024 (arXiv:2404.11262) SaMIA sampling-based pseudo-likelihood MIA

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean ROUGE-N recall (optionally zlib-weighted) so members score higher.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by whether the target record is in the target client's local data. After Flower (flwr) FedAvg fine-tuning, prompt the final FL model with the target record's prefix, sample num_samples continuations, and score the mean ROUGE-N recall against the held-out suffix. No reference model is used (black-box).
methodology.paper_attack: SaMIA (Kaneko et al., 2024): split the target text into a prefix and a reference suffix, sample m continuations from the model given the prefix, and score membership by the mean ROUGE-N recall of the candidates against the true suffix; the SaMIA x zlib variant weights each candidate by its zlib bit length. Fully black-box (generation only, no likelihoods).
methodology.deviation_from_source: SaMIA is defined for pre-trained LLMs on WikiMIA; here it is transferred to federated fine-tuning, attacking a memorized fine-tuning record via black-box generation. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy transition model whose generation reproduces the suffix only when the target record was in training; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and true sampling.

config.paper_source: Fu et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.06062) SPV-MIA: self-prompt calibration + probabilistic variation

methodology.deviation_from_source: SPV-MIA already targets the fine-tuning phase; this transfers it to FEDERATED fine-tuning. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer whose prob/generate/paraphrase mimic memorization and self-prompting; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM (Flower FedAvg), a self-prompt reference fine-tuned on the target's generations, and (optionally) a T5 mask-and-reconstruct paraphraser in place of the pure-Python token masking.
methodology.paper_attack: SPV-MIA: (1) self-prompt reference model theta_dot fine-tuned on text the target LLM itself generates from short public prompts (practical difficulty calibration); (2) probabilistic variation assessment detecting whether a record is a local maximum of the model's probability via symmetric paraphrases. Decision A = 1[p_tilde_theta(x) - p_tilde_theta_dot(x) >= tau].
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; primary paper metric AUC (roc_auc). spv_membership_score = pv_theta - pv_theta_dot with pv = prob_x - mean(paraphrase_probs) = -p_tilde (paper Eq. 10 sign flipped so higher => member).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation produces theta, the self-prompt reference theta_dot is bootstrapped by prompting theta to generate a self-dataset and fitting a second model on it. The target record's probabilistic variation (prob(x) - mean(prob(paraphrases))) is measured under theta and theta_dot and combined as pv_theta - pv_theta_dot.

config.paper_source: Shi et al. 2024 (ICLR / arXiv:2310.16789) Min-K% Prob reference-free MIA

methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.

methodology.paper_attack: Yeom et al.'s LOSS membership inference predicts membership when the target model assigns a candidate example unusually low loss; the advantage is linked to the training-vs-held-out generalization gap.
methodology.attacker_observation: Final FL global model probabilities/logits sufficient to compute per-token NLL.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Federated clients locally fine-tune an open-source causal LM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg strategy via run_simulation. Positive and negative worlds differ by whether the target client includes the target sequence. The server/adversary scores the final FL model's average per-token NLL on the target sequence and thresholds the loss using calibration non-members.
methodology.deviation_from_source: The original paper evaluates classical supervised models. This notebook preserves the LOSS decision rule but moves the training process to FedAvg-based causal-LM fine-tuning.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; lower loss predicts membership.

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = -(log_perplexity / zlib_entropy_bits) so members score higher.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Carlini et al. flag fine-tuning as future work, so applying the zlib ratio to a fine-tuned model is a transfer of their pre-training signal. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.paper_attack: zlib-entropy ratio MIA: rank candidates by log_perplexity / len(zlib.compress(text)); zlib is a model-independent reference that down-ranks repetitive/boilerplate text.

methodology.deviation_from_source: The Min-K%++ paper (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025) targets pre-training-data detection and runs no fine-tuning MIA; this notebook transfers the logit-z-score statistic to a fine-tuned FL model, where multi-epoch memorization should make member tokens stronger modes. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer that emits per-token pseudo-distributions; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation and real log-softmax logits.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K%++ reference-free MIA: per token z_t = (log p(x_t|x_<t) - mu_t) / sigma_t with mu_t = sum_z p(z) log p(z) and sigma_t = sqrt(sum_z p(z) log p(z)^2 - mu_t^2) over the full softmax; score = mean of the K% smallest z_t; higher => member. Grey-box (needs full logits).
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, run the target record through the final FL model only, read the full per-position vocabulary distribution, compute the per-token z-scores, and average the K% smallest. Reference-free: no second model.
methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of K% smallest per-token z-scores so members (whose tokens are modes) score higher.

privacy_accounting.scope: Training releases in this experiment only; audit scores, probe training, private retrieval outputs and repeated experiments are not covered.

methodology.metric_definition: Adv = 0.5 * TPR + 0.5 * TNR; membership score = mean of the k% lowest per-token log-probs so members score higher. AUC is the paper's threshold-free headline metric.
methodology.deviation_from_source: Shi et al. Section 6 fine-tunes LLaMA-7B for one epoch and detects contaminated examples with Min-K% Prob (AUC 0.91), so applying Min-K% to a federated fine-tuned model is a direct transfer. The smoke run uses a deterministic toy causal scorer exposing per-token log-probs; set use_hf_models=True for genuine federated fine-tuning of an open-source LLM with the Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation.
methodology.llm_adaptation: Positive and negative FL worlds differ by target-client membership; after Flower (flwr) FedAvg simulation, score the target record under the final FL model only by averaging the k% lowest per-token log-probs. No reference model is used.
methodology.paper_attack: Min-K% Prob (Shi et al. 2024): compute per-token log p(x_i | x_<i), select the k% lowest-probability tokens, and average their log-likelihood. Reference-free; a member has few very low-probability tokens so its Min-K% average stays high.

privacy_accounting.scope: Training releases in this experiment only; audit scores, probe training, private retrieval outputs and repeated experiments are not covered.
